text:
Sam: planning a quick canary for the 'orbit' kernel + slim-quant profile tonight. target window 23:00-00:30 UTC. who can own canary + smoke? rollback readiness?

Ivy: I can take canary ownership 23:00-00:00 UTC. will be oncall and available in thread.

Miguel: I’ll own rollback/runbooks/alerts. quick Q: how big is the slab and which model(s) are we testing?

Sam: start tiny — 5% slab in eu-west. models: rdlm-medium primary, rdlm-tiny fallback. deploy CLI: `rb deploy --canary orbit-kernel:v2 --slice 5% --region eu-west`

Nora: I’ll run smoke scripts and post logs. ping me 15m before start. sample smoke I’ll use:
```bash
# smoke.sh
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rdlm-medium","input":"hello"}' | jq .
```

Miguel: alert thresholds I care about: latency > 1500ms (p50->p90 delta), token error rate > 0.5% over a 5m window. if either triggers -> rollback. I’ll create 2 grafana alerts + a PD service. also recommend routing flag `--fallback-model rdlm-tiny`.

deploy-bot: Canary started on eu-west 5% slab by @Sam at 3456789400 UTC.

Ivy: saw a tiny spike ~23:07, one slot threw a transient 500, overall error rate still <0.2%. continuing to monitor. :ok_hand:

Nora: smoke results: 20/20 sanity checks passed, responses look fine. uploading logs to the shared folder (link posted).

ci-bot: smoke pipeline run #782 succeeded (tests: 12 passed, 0 failed).

Miguel: rollback command (keeps it quick): `rb rollback orbit-kernel:v2 --to orbit-kernel:v1 --force` — I’ve tested that in staging. I’ll standby to execute if alerts fire or if we see quality regressions.

Sam: plan: if canary stable -> ramp to 20% at 23:40, then to 100% at 00:10 UTC. if any red flags, call rollback + @Miguel immediately.

Ivy: I can do the 23:40 ramp up to 20% if we get a green at 23:20. :thumbsup:

Nora: I’ll run end-to-end chatflow tests at 23:30 and post a short summary in this thread (latency, hallucination quick checks).

deploy-bot: Canary ramp to 20% scheduled at 23:40 UTC (manual approval pending).

Sam: leaving this thread — reachable by phone if needed. thanks team; short and sharp.
